subject.title: Agent-scoped tools.allow may not restrict built-in tools in the provider-visible tool set

question: Should a non-empty per-agent `tools.allow` be exclusive for every provider-visible tool, or are named built-in/forced tools intentionally exempt?
rationale: The correct repair boundary depends on the intended authorization contract; source-level similarity to the bundled-tool fix cannot safely decide whether a forced-tool exception is deliberate.

options.title: Make allowlists exclusive
options.body: Apply the resolved policy to the complete final provider-visible set and add regression coverage for all construction branches.

options.title: Document forced-tool exceptions
options.body: Retain only explicitly approved forced tools, document their rationale, and test that every other built-in and plugin tool remains restricted.

options.title: Preserve current split behavior
options.body: Keep branch-specific filtering only if maintainers can document why provider-visible built-in/plugin tools are intentionally outside this agent policy.

recommendation.title: Make allowlists exclusive
recommendation.body: Apply the resolved policy to the complete final provider-visible set and add regression coverage for all construction branches.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged final-policy work is the strongest available history connection to the final tool-list policy boundary.
